# Cost model (generated by `python cost/cost_model.py`)

Prices: AWS Price List API, us-east-1, snapshot in `cost/aws_prices.json` (SKU + publication date per line).

## Inputs

| Input | Value | Label | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| events_per_day | 50,000,000 | Brief | brief: ~50M events/day |
| spike_multiplier | 10 | Brief | brief: 10x traffic spikes |
| fixture_mean_bytes | 230 | Observed | mean line size of fixtures/event_sample.jsonl (25 rows) |
| event_bytes | 1,024 | Assumed | real events carry user agent, full URLs, custom props; 4x the fixture |
| compression | 5 | Assumed | gzip on S3 and ClickHouse column compression on JSON-like events |
| retention_months | 13 | Assumed | 13 months raw + hot, so year-over-year dashboards work |
| kinesis_headroom | 2 | Assumed | 2x over the 10x peak for uneven partition keys |
| collector_req_per_task | 1,000 | Assumed | per 1 vCPU Node task; local Python prototype did 3,000 req/s on one process (Observed, results/) |
| collector_tasks_avg | 8 | Estimated | autoscale 4..12; peak 5,787 req/s / 1,000 = 6, +2 for AZ spread |
| lambda_batch_avg | 50 | Estimated | ~48 records/shard/s at average load with a 1s batching window |
| lambda_seconds | 0.2 | Assumed | per batch, includes Redis and ClickHouse round trips |
| lambda_gb | 1.0 | Assumed | memory size |
| alb_lcu_avg | 24 | Estimated | worst case one new TLS connection per beacon: ~600 new conn/s / 25 per LCU |
| query_tasks | 4 | Assumed | dashboard + personalization decision API, 1 vCPU / 2 GB each |
| log_gb | 100 | Assumed | batch-level logs only; per-event logging would be ~1,430 GB |
| bigquery_share | 0.2 | Assumed | share of export volume going cross-cloud to BigQuery |
| staging_share | 0.25 | Assumed | staging env as a share of compute |

Derived: average 579 ev/s, 10x peak 5,787 ev/s, 1,431 GB/month ingested, 3,719 GB retained (all Estimated from the inputs above).

## Alternatives priced and rejected

- Kinesis on-demand instead of provisioned: about $258/month (Estimated). Cheaper to run, but AWS documents that on-demand only absorbs up to double the previous 30-day peak and can throttle when traffic more than doubles within 15 minutes. A 10x Black Friday spike breaks that rule, so provisioned shards sized for 10x win.
- Logging every event to CloudWatch would add about $715/month (Estimated). Batch-level logs only.
- Firehose bills Kinesis-sourced records in 5 KB steps, so a 1 KB event is billed as 5 KB. Still small here; noted so nobody is surprised.
- ClickHouse Cloud (managed) instead of self-managed EC2: not priced here (no public AWS price list). It trades money for team time, which is the scarcer resource. A procurement decision, see SUBMISSION.md.
